question: Will a finalized firm Boeing purchase agreement with a Chinese buyer be publicly confirmed as of October 1, 2026?

calls.reasoning: Status quo (no firm contract) has held 129 of 139 window days; only ~7 qualifying Chinese firm aircraft (China Southern freighters, June 2026) exist since May 15, so YES needs a ~93+ aircraft definitive contract signed and unambiguously reported within 10 days. Boeing's Orders & Deliveries route is mechanically unavailable (Sept data publishes ~Oct 13, after the Oct 1 deadline), so only press reporting of a signed/definitive contract can resolve YES. Ortberg on Sept 16 explicitly tempered summit expectations ('we didn't get an order for 200'), described orders as incremental and airline-by-airline pending NDRC allocation, and did so at cost to the stock — a costly signal from the best-informed party. The Sept 24 Xi state visit is a genuine catalyst and Trump wants a pre-midterm deliverable, but summit-announced China-Boeing deals historically arrive as 'orders and commitments' (Nov 2017 CASC 300-jet deal, split never disclosed), and the fine print resolves genuinely conflicting reporting as NO. Decomposition: ~60% chance of some Boeing announcement at/after the summit x ~20-25% that it is reported as a definitive signed contract for >=100, plus ~2% for non-summit airline orders.

calls.reconciliation: Five disputes. FACTUAL: (a) whether the O&D path is open — Run 3's claim that Boeing's O&D tool refreshes weekly on Tuesdays (last inside window: Sept 29) is likely correct and Runs 1/2 overstated closure, but all three dossiers agree Boeing books large China orders under 'Unidentified Customer(s)', which is not attribution to a Chinese customer, so the path stays near-closed either way; (b) how many qualifying firm aircraft already exist — only Run 1 located the June 2026 China Southern Air Logistics order (5x 777-8F + 2x 777F = 7); Runs 2/3 found none, which is compatible rather than conflicting, so ~7 of 100 stands; (c) market anchor — all three independently found no matched contract on Polymarket, Manifold, Kalshi or bookmakers (Kalshi prices quarterly delivery counts, a different resolution object), so there is nothing to blend. JUDGMENT: (d) P(summit yields any Boeing order event) — Run 1 ~60% vs Run 3 ~30-35%; no run found a published deliverables list or confirmed signing ceremony despite all three searching for one, and previews (CSIS, ASPI, Heritage, CNBC) name export controls and the truce extension instead, so I take ~45%; (e) P(firm/definitive reporting | announcement) — Run 1 20-25% vs Run 3 50-60%; I side near Run 1 on three reconciled facts: the Nov 2017 CASC deal was released by Boeing as 'orders and commitments' with the split never disclosed, SCMP (Sept 20) has the 'what' (model mix) still open so slots/pricing are unsettled days before any signing, and Ortberg's Sept 16 incremental airline-by-airline framing means an announcement likely falls short of 100 firm in one instrument. That conditional is pure judgment; no evidence in the dossiers breaks it, and I take the reading I would bet on. 0.45 x 0.20 + ~0.02 non-summit ~= 0.10 — below all three runs because the ambiguity clause is a one-way drag that compounds with the model-mix fact, not a symmetric uncertainty.
